items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I'd show up in there because Alphonse Pico was the one who started calling me Rat.

ctx.x: You could have had the hat to the hole in the bottom. Yeah, yeah, they called me Rat.
I'd show up in there because Alphonse Pico was the one who started calling me Rat.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: And he had, uh, uh, Alphonse Piku.

ctx.x: And you remember who else was in the band with Oliver when you worked with him and where

you played? Uh, let's see now. We played so many different, we was playing spot job. We didn't have no sound plays until we went to Hunson Nagel. Now, uh, let's see. What color was this, Hunson Nagel? He had, uh, Liberty in the Outerville. Liberty. He's band, he had, uh, uh, Call it the Casino. Oh yeah. He had, uh, Chris Kelly. Uh, no, uh, he had, uh, uh, Chris Miner on the drum. And he had, uh, uh, Alphonse Piku. And, uh, Joe Atkins. Uh, Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Ed Atkins. Ed Atkins was, yeah.…
That was the Magnolia band. Do you remember, uh, I think, uh, Louie Kepard tells me that he played in the Magnolia band too with Oliver for a while.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: No, just Peek Good and Eddie Atkins was playing trombone, you know, I think. That's been a long time. Eddie Atkins and Piku. That was the Magnolia Band.

ctx.x: Any other clarinet player of them?
No. No, just Peek Good and Eddie Atkins was playing trombone, you know, I think. That's been a long time. Eddie Atkins and Piku. That was the Magnolia Band.
Mm-hmm. I thought you said there was a little dog fellow there on clarinet at one time.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I played with Piku out there too.

ctx.x: He played that Dixieland and jazz trumpet just like the rest of them. Yeah. They all have to play that same way, you see, when you play the trumpet. Because when you get in a band, if you're playing trumpet in a band like they was playing then, you'd have to play that style, you know? The only difference was some fellas could play in brass band music and they couldn't play dance music, you see. That's the two different types of music, you see. When there's a straight and a jazz the other way to dance and music,…

Well, I read Piku told us something about playing out there too with Manuel Perez. Oh, yeah, yeah. I played with Piku out there too. Piku said he remembers the same time when Freddie picked up the cornet sometime.
Yeah, yeah. Was it a pic on that same gap with you, Willie?
